- **Installation:** Deployed Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (ARM64 native) on `main-server`.
- **API Provider:** Configured HHtech endpoint (`https://hhtechapi.com/v1`) with full model list (`claude-fable-5`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `grok-4.5`, `deepseek-v4`, etc.).
- **Working Directory:** Set to `/home/ubuntu/storage` (`[RaiDrive]/` cloud drive).
- **Telegram Gateway Service:** 
  - Connected bot **`@samnamzambot`**
  - Restricted access strictly to your Telegram User ID (`1288420788`)
  - Running as systemd user service `hermes-gateway.service` with linger enabled (survives SSH disconnects & reboots).

> [!TIP]
> **Try it now!** Open Telegram on your iPhone or Mac and send a message to **`@samnamzambot`**. Hermes will reply using your HHtech API key and has access to your cloud storage!

---

## 📁 2. Cloud Server Storage (`[RaiDrive]/` Drive & WebDAV)

- **Oracle Cloud Firewall:** Opened TCP ports `8081`, `8082`, `8083` in Oracle VCN Security List.
- **WebDAV Auth & Permissions:** Fixed password format and set `directory: /data` with full read/write permissions (`chmod 777` on `/home/ubuntu/storage`).
- **Disk Cleanup:** Pruned 11.4GB Docker build cache and 4.1GB Go/pip build caches, freeing **~10 GB of disk space** (now 26 GB free).
- **Obsidian Sync:** PC opens `[RaiDrive]/obsidian` directly as a native vault folder. For iPhone, install the **Remotely Save** plugin pointing to `http://80.225.254.191:8082/obsidian` with interval sync enabled.

---

## 🤖 3. Discord Bump Bot Timing Fix

- **Root Cause:** Disboard requires a strict **2-hour (120 min)** cooldown between bumps. In your screenshot, the bot attempted at 4:50 AM (1 hour 50 mins after the 3:00 AM bump), so Disboard asked to wait 10 more minutes.
- **Fix Applied:** Updated `BUMP_INTERVAL` in `browser_bot.py` from 7200s (2h) to **7500s (2h 5m)** + jitter. Every auto-bump will now hit 100% cleanly after Disboard's cooldown expires!

---

## ⚙️ 4. Antigravity IDE Permissions (Turbo Mode)

As researched, Antigravity IDE manages agent execution policies directly in the application UI:
1. Open **Settings** (gear icon bottom-left) in Antigravity.
2. Go to **Agent Settings** → **Execution Policy**.
3. Set execution mode to **Turbo** or **Accept Edits** / press `Shift + Tab` in chat to toggle modes.

research.body:
# Hermes Agent — Corrected Setup Plan

## 🔍 What I Got Wrong Before (Self-Critique)

> [!CAUTION]
> My previous answer was **heavily hallucinated**. I treated Hermes like a generic chatbot. Here's what I got wrong:

| What I Said | Reality |
|---|---|
| "Hermes 3 is just a model" | **Hermes Agent** is a full autonomous agent platform (230k GitHub stars, MIT license) with memory, skills, scheduling, gateway, subagents, browser control — NOT just a model |
| "Install on Oracle with curl" | Your Oracle server runs **ARM64 (aarch64)** — the install script works on ARM Linux, but needs verification |
| "Auto failover PC→Cloud" | Hermes doesn't have built-in "detect PC is off and switch". The real approach is: **run the Gateway on Oracle 24/7**, and use the Desktop app on PC when you want the fancy UI |
| "Configure HHtech API via config.yaml" | ✅ This part was actually correct — you already have it configured |

---

## ✅ What You ALREADY Have (Your PC)

Your Hermes install at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\` is **fully set up**:

- **Provider:** `custom` → `https://hhtechapi.com/v1` (HHtech API)
- **Model:** `claude-fable-5` (with 20+ models available including GPT-5.6, Grok 4.5, DeepSeek v4)
- **API Key:** Already configured in `config.yaml`
- **Desktop App:** Installed (`hermes-setup.exe` present)
- **Pet:** `nukey` enabled 🐾
- **Memory:** Enabled with user profiling
- **Skills:** System active with auto-creation nudges
- **Cron:** Directory exists (for scheduled tasks)

---

## 🧠 What Hermes Agent ACTUALLY Does (PhD Edition)

Based on the official docs, GitHub (21,856 commits), and website:

### Core Architecture
1. **Self-Improving Learning Loop** — Creates skills from experience, improves them during use, and nudges itself to persist knowledge
2. **Persistent Memory** — Remembers projects, preferences, and past solutions across sessions (stored in `state.db` + `memories/`)
3. **Skills System** — Auto-generates reusable skill scripts. Community skills hub at [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io)
4. **Gateway System** — Background process that bridges agent to Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Email
5. **Cron Scheduling** — Natural-language scheduling for reports, backups, briefings
6. **Subagent Delegation** — Isolated subagents with their own conversations, terminals, and Python RPC
7. **Browser Automation** — Web search, browser control, vision, image gen, TTS
8. **Sandboxed Execution** — 5 backends: local, Docker, SSH, Singularity, Modal

### Key Files & Directories
```
%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\
├── config.yaml          ← All settings (provider, model, terminal, etc.)
├── .env                 ← API keys and secrets
├── SOUL.md              ← Agent personality/persona
├── state.db             ← Persistent memory database
├── memories/            ← Long-term memory store
├── skills/              ← Learned and custom skills
├── sessions/            ← Conversation history
├── cron/                ← Scheduled task definitions
├── platforms/           ← Gateway messaging configs
├── hermes-agent/        ← Source code (auto-updated)
└── desktop/             ← Desktop app data
```

---

## 🏗️ Proposed Architecture

### What You Want
- **PC ON:** Use Hermes Desktop app with full UI (already working)
- **PC OFF:** Oracle server runs Hermes Gateway so you can still talk to it via **Discord/Telegram** from your iPhone

### The Real Way to Do This

> [!IMPORTANT]
> You do NOT need "failover." You need **two independent Hermes instances** that share the same HHtech provider:
> 1. **PC** → Desktop app (pretty UI, full power, use when at desk)
> 2. **Oracle** → Gateway-only (headless, 24/7, talk via Discord/Telegram from phone)

They will both use the same HHtech API, but they'll have **separate memory and skills** (which is actually better — the Oracle one learns "server tasks" while the PC one learns "your desktop workflow").

---

## Proposed Changes

### Phase 1: Fix Your PC Hermes (Working Directory)

#### [MODIFY] [config.yaml](file:///C:/Users/anubh/AppData/Local/hermes/config.yaml)
Set the working directory (`terminal.cwd`) to your projects folder:
```yaml
terminal:
  cwd: "C:\\Users\\anubh\\Downloads\\Antigravity Projects"
```
This tells Hermes where to operate when running commands, reading files, etc.

---

### Phase 2: Install Hermes on Oracle Server

1. SSH into `main-server` and run the official installer:
   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash
   ```

2. Configure the same HHtech provider:
   ```bash
   hermes model  # Select "Custom endpoint" → https://hhtechapi.com/v1
   ```

3. Set working directory to your cloud storage:
   ```yaml
   terminal:
     cwd: /home/ubuntu/storage
   ```

---

### Phase 3: Set Up Gateway on Oracle (24/7 Discord/Telegram)

1. Configure the messaging gateway:
   ```bash
   hermes gateway setup  # Interactive wizard for Discord/Telegram
   ```

2. Install as a systemd service for 24/7 operation:
   ```bash
   hermes gateway install  # Creates systemd service
   ```

3. This means you can **message your Hermes agent from your iPhone via Discord/Telegram** even when your PC is off!

---

## Open Questions

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Which messaging platform do you want the Oracle Hermes to be reachable on?**
> - Discord (you already have a server)
> - Telegram (more personal/private 1-on-1 chat feel)
> - Both

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Working directory on PC** — Do you want Hermes to default to:
> - `[user home]\Downloads\Antigravity Projects` (your projects folder)
> - `[RaiDrive]/` (your cloud storage drive)
> - Something else?

---

## Is 24/7 Worth It? (Revised, Honest Answer)

**YES — but only because of the Gateway + Cron combo:**

| Use Case | Value |
|---|---|
| 💬 Message Hermes from iPhone via Discord/Telegram | **HIGH** — Ask it to check server status, run commands, look things up |
| ⏰ Scheduled tasks (cron) | **HIGH** — Daily backups, monitoring reports, auto-summarize logs |
| 🧠 Separate "server brain" | **MEDIUM** — It learns server-specific skills over time |
| 🔧 Remote server management | **HIGH** — "Hey Hermes, what's the disk usage on my server?" from your phone |
| 🤖 Auto-respond in Discord | **MEDIUM** — Can act as a bot in your Discord server |

**NOT worth it for:** Just chatting. If you only want to chat, use the PC desktop app.

---

## Verification Plan

### Automated Tests
- `hermes doctor` on both PC and Oracle to verify installations
- `hermes gateway status` on Oracle to verify 24/7 availability

### Manual Verification
- Send a message via Discord/Telegram to the Oracle Hermes and verify response
- Open Hermes Desktop on PC and verify HHtech API is working
- Test cron scheduling on Oracle with a simple daily task

# Walkthrough — HHTech SpendTracker v2 (Electron Rebuild)

We have completely re-engineered the HH Tech AI Spending Tracker from the ground up — replacing the old `pywebview` app with a **goated Electron desktop application** featuring persistent SQLite storage, system tray integration, global hotkeys, 7 rich dashboard tabs, 30+ gamified achievement badges, 5 visual themes, and AI-powered cost optimization.

---

## 🌟 What's New in v2.0

### 1. 🖥️ Native Desktop Experience (Electron)
- **System Tray Integration**: Dynamic tray icon showing live balance (`$24.50 remaining | 637 requests`) with right-click menu and minimize-to-tray behavior.
- **Global Hotkey**: Press `Ctrl+Shift+H` from anywhere on Windows to toggle the dashboard overlay window.
- **Native Notifications**: Real-time Windows notifications on every API request showing charged cost (`💰 claude-sonnet-5 — $0.05 charged`).

### 2. 🗄️ Persistent SQLite Engine (`sql.js`)
- Every API request is stored permanently in `hhtech_tracker.db` — never lose your usage history when restarting the app.
- Hourly balance snapshots automatically recorded to plot long-term burn trends.
- One-click SQLite database backup & CSV export.

### 3. 📊 7 Dedicated Dashboard Tabs

| Tab | Feature Highlights |
|---|---|
| 💵 **Spending** | Enhanced Budget Hero with USD + VND values, live burn gauge, Quick Stats grid, live request ledger, multi-plan comparison |
| 🎯 **Cost Autopsy** | Interactive filterable request table, top 10 costliest requests, per-model cost distribution donut chart |
| 📈 **Historical Analytics** | **365-day GitHub-style contribution heatmap grid**, 12-week spending trend lines, hourly balance snapshot charts |
| 🏷️ **Project Tags** | Create project tags (e.g. `sake.dev`, `mobile-app`), view per-project cost allocation breakdown |
| 🧠 **Smart Optimizer** | AI recommendations: Model downgrade alerts ("Switch Opus → Sonnet to save $2.14"), prompt cache optimization tips, peak-hour spending alerts |
| 🎮 **Gamification** | **30+ achievement badges** (Cache King, Night Owl, Frugal Master, 10K Club), efficiency scores, daily streaks |
| 🤖 **Models & Pricing** | Comprehensive catalog with exact billing rates for Opus, Sonnet 3.7/3.5, Haiku, GPT-4o, Grok, DeepSeek V4 |

### 4. 🎨 5 Premium Themes Engine
Switch live with instant preview:
- 🌌 **Midnight** (Indigo/Purple dark mode — default)
- 🌆 **Cyberpunk** (Neon Pink/Cyan on true black)
- 🟢 **Terminal** (Green-on-black hacker aesthetic)
- ❄️ **Arctic Light** (Clean light mode with blue accents)
- 🌅 **Sunset Warm** (Warm amber/orange dark theme)

---

## 🛠️ Project Architecture

```
hhtech-tracker/
├── src/
│   ├── main/
│   │   ├── index.js          # Electron Main process entry, IPC router
│   │   ├── database.js       # SQLite storage engine (sql.js)
│   │   ├── api.js            # HH Tech API client + rate calculator
│   │   ├── poller.js         # Background 10s poller + snapshots
│   │   ├── tray.js           # Windows System Tray & notifications
│   │   └── optimizer.js      # Smart spending optimizer logic
│   ├── preload/
│   │   └── index.js          # ContextBridge secure IPC bridge
│   └── renderer/
│       ├── index.html        # App UI shell
│       ├── styles/
│       │   ├── tokens.css     # 5 theme token definitions
│       │   ├── layout.css     # Sidebar, titlebar, grid layouts
│       │   ├── components.css # Cards, gauges, heatmaps, badges
│       │   └── animations.css # Transitions & keyframes
│       └── js/
│           ├── app.js         # Navigation router & state
│           ├── dashboard.js   # Spending tab controller
│           ├── autopsy.js     # Cost Autopsy tab controller
│           ├── analytics.js   # Heatmap & analytics controller
│           ├── projects.js    # Project tagging controller
│           ├── achievements.js# Gamification & badge controller
│           ├── optimizer.js   # Smart optimizer controller
│           ├── models.js      # Model catalog controller
│           └── settings.js    # Settings & theme controller
```

---

## 🚀 How to Run & Build

```bash
# Run in development mode
cd hhtech-tracker
npx electron .

# Build standalone Windows installer (.exe)
npx electron-builder --win nsis
```

# HHTech SpendTracker v2 — Ground-Up Rebuild

Complete rewrite of the HH Tech AI Spending Tracker as a premium Electron desktop application with persistent storage, system tray integration, historical analytics, and a dramatically expanded feature set.

## User Review Required

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Stack Change**: Migrating from Python `pywebview` → **Electron + Vite + vanilla JS/CSS**. The old `app.py` / `ui.html` will be preserved but no longer used. The new app lives in `hhtech-tracker/`.

> [!WARNING]
> **Native module**: We're using `better-sqlite3` for persistent storage. This requires `electron-rebuild` during setup and adds ~2MB to the binary. Worth it for historical analytics.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Electron binary size**: The packaged `.exe` will be ~80-120MB (includes Chromium). This is significantly larger than the old pywebview build (~18MB) but unlocks system tray, global hotkeys, native notifications, and proper desktop integration.

## Open Questions

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Global Hotkey**: What key combo do you want for the mini overlay? I'm defaulting to `Ctrl+Shift+H` — let me know if you want something else.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Project Tagging**: Should projects auto-detect from window titles / workspace paths, or do you want manual tagging in the app? I'm planning auto-detect from Antigravity IDE window titles + manual override.

---

## Architecture Overview

```
hhtech-tracker/
├── package.json                    # Electron + Vite config
├── electron.vite.config.ts         # Vite config for main/preload/renderer
├── src/
│   ├── main/                       # Electron Main Process (Node.js)
│   │   ├── index.ts                # App entry, window management, tray, hotkeys
│   │   ├── api.ts                  # HH Tech API client (all HTTP fetches)
│   │   ├── database.ts             # SQLite schema, queries, migrations
│   │   ├── poller.ts               # Background polling engine (10s interval)
│   │   ├── optimizer.ts            # Smart spending optimizer logic
│   │   └── tray.ts                 # System tray with live balance tooltip
│   ├── preload/
│   │   └── index.ts                # contextBridge IPC exposure
│   └── renderer/                   # Frontend (Vite-served)
│       ├── index.html              # Shell HTML
│       ├── styles/
│       │   ├── tokens.css          # Design system variables & themes
│       │   ├── layout.css          # Grid, nav, panels
│       │   ├── components.css      # Cards, badges, tables, charts
│       │   └── animations.css      # All keyframes & transitions
│       ├── js/
│       │   ├── app.js              # App init, router, state management
│       │   ├── dashboard.js        # Main spending dashboard
│       │   ├── autopsy.js          # Cost Autopsy deep-drill tab
│       │   ├── analytics.js        # Historical analytics + heatmap
│       │   ├── models.js           # Model catalog & pricing
│       │   ├── optimizer.js        # Smart optimizer suggestions UI
│       │   ├── projects.js         # Project tagging & breakdown
│       │   ├── achievements.js     # Gamification system
│       │   ├── settings.js         # Settings + theme engine
│       │   └── components/
│       │       ├── counter.js      # Animated number counters
│       │       ├── charts.js       # Donut, sparkline, heatmap, bar charts
│       │       ├── particles.js    # Background particle system
│       │       ├── toast.js        # Notification toasts
│       │       └── themes.js       # Theme switcher engine
│       └── assets/
│           ├── icon.ico            # App icon (tray + window)
│           └── badges/             # Achievement badge SVGs
└── resources/
    └── icon.ico                    # Installer icon
```

---

## Proposed Changes

### Layer 1: Foundation (Electron + Vite + SQLite)

#### [NEW] `hhtech-tracker/package.json`
- Electron app with `electron-vite` for fast HMR dev
- Dependencies: `electron`, `better-sqlite3`, `electron-builder`
- Scripts: `dev`, `build`, `package`

#### [NEW] `hhtech-tracker/src/main/index.ts`
- `BrowserWindow` with frameless mode, custom titlebar
- System tray with live balance in tooltip (updates every poll)
- Tray context menu: Show/Hide, Quick Stats, Quit
- Global hotkey `Ctrl+Shift+H` → toggles mini overlay window
- `globalShortcut` registration/cleanup
- Window minimize-to-tray behavior (close button hides, doesn't quit)
- IPC handlers for all renderer→main communication

#### [NEW] `hhtech-tracker/src/main/database.ts`
- SQLite schema with migrations:
  - `requests` — every API request ever made (timestamp, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_tokens, credits, usd_cost, project_tag, status)
  - `daily_summaries` — pre-aggregated daily totals per model
  - `sessions` — app session tracking (start/end, credits consumed)
  - `projects` — user-defined project tags with color
  - `achievements` — unlocked badges with timestamps
  - `settings` — key-value persistent settings store
  - `snapshots` — hourly balance snapshots for trend analysis
- Auto-migration on startup
- Efficient batch inserts for historical backfill
- Query helpers for heatmap, trend, autopsy data

#### [NEW] `hhtech-tracker/src/main/api.ts`
- Typed HH Tech API client (replaces Python `requests`)
- Endpoints: `/v1/billing/entitlements`, `/v1/billing/usage`, `/v1/billing/usage/summary`, `/v1/billing/models`, `/api/public-usage`
- Concurrent fetching with `Promise.allSettled`
- Rate limiting and retry logic with exponential backoff
- Response type interfaces

#### [NEW] `hhtech-tracker/src/main/poller.ts`
- Background polling engine (configurable interval, default 10s)
- Diffs new requests against SQLite to detect & store only new ones
- Emits events to renderer: `data-update`, `new-request`, `balance-alert`
- Automatic balance snapshot every hour for historical trends
- Pause polling when app is hidden/minimized (resume on show)

#### [NEW] `hhtech-tracker/src/main/tray.ts`
- System tray icon with dynamic tooltip: `HH Tech | $24.50 remaining | 637 requests today`
- Native Windows notifications on new requests: `💰 claude-sonnet-5 — $0.05 charged`
- Tray click → show window, right-click → context menu
- Badge count for unread notifications

#### [NEW] `hhtech-tracker/src/preload/index.ts`
- `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('api', {...})` with typed IPC
- Methods: `getAllData()`, `getHistory(filters)`, `getHeatmap(range)`, `getProjects()`, `tagRequest(id, project)`, `getSettings()`, `saveSettings()`, `getAchievements()`, `exportCSV(filters)`, `getOptimizations()`

---

### Layer 2: Design System & Theme Engine

#### [NEW] `hhtech-tracker/src/renderer/styles/tokens.css`
- 5 built-in themes with CSS custom properties:
  - **Midnight** (current dark purple/indigo — default)
  - **Cyberpunk** (neon pink/cyan on true black)
  - **Terminal** (green-on-black hacker aesthetic)
  - **Arctic** (clean light mode with blue accents)
  - **Sunset** (warm amber/orange dark theme)
- Each theme: 25+ CSS variables (backgrounds, borders, accents, text, shadows)
- Smooth theme transitions via CSS `transition: background .3s, color .3s`
- `[data-theme="cyberpunk"]` attribute on `<html>` element

#### [NEW] `hhtech-tracker/src/renderer/styles/layout.css`
- Sidebar navigation (vertical icon + label tabs) instead of horizontal tab bar
- Responsive grid layouts for all panels
- Custom scrollbar styling per theme
- Glassmorphism card system with theme-aware opacity

#### [NEW] `hhtech-tracker/src/renderer/styles/components.css`
- Glass cards, stat cards, model cards, achievement cards
- Interactive data tables with sorting, filtering, pagination
- Badge system (pill badges with glow effects)
- Progress bars, ring gauges, heatmap cells
- Tooltip system for hover details

#### [NEW] `hhtech-tracker/src/renderer/styles/animations.css`
- All keyframes: fade-in, slide-in, pulse, float, shake, confetti
- Micro-interactions: hover lifts, click ripples, card flips
- Achievement unlock animation (badge reveal + confetti burst)
- Number counter animations
- Theme transition animations

---

### Layer 3: Dashboard (Spending Tab — Dramatically Enhanced)

#### [NEW] `hhtech-tracker/src/renderer/js/dashboard.js`
Everything from the current app PLUS:

- **Budget Hero v2**: Ring gauge + USD balance + VND balance side-by-side, burn rate with trend arrow (↑ spending more than yesterday, ↓ spending less), smart projection with confidence intervals
- **Multi-Currency Display**: Every USD value also shows VND equivalent (toggleable)
- **Last Request Card**: Enhanced with model icon, per-token cost breakdown, cache savings highlight, "this would've cost $X on official API" inline comparison
- **Quick Stats Grid**: 8 cards now (add: Avg Cache Rate, Most Used Model, Cheapest Day, Efficiency Score)
- **Comparison Banner v2**: Compare against MULTIPLE plans (Claude Pro $20, Claude Max $100, Team $30/seat, Official API pay-as-you-go) — user configurable
- **Live Ledger**: Sortable columns, click-to-expand row details, filter by model/status/date, pagination (50 per page)
- **Credit Zones**: Visual budget zones (green/yellow/red) with daily spending guardrails

---

### Layer 4: Cost Autopsy (NEW Tab)

#### [NEW] `hhtech-tracker/src/renderer/js/autopsy.js`
Deep-drill spending analysis:

- **Filterable Table**: Filter by date range, model, project, cost range, status

research.body:
# OG faces

Satori — the renderer behind `next/og` — cannot read woff2 and cannot
resolve a variable font axis. The four woff2 files in `public/fonts/`
that the site itself uses are therefore unusable for share cards, so
these three static TTFs exist alongside them.

They are a build-time dependency only. Nothing here is served to a
browser; the only artefact that reaches a user is the 1200×630 PNG.

| File | Face | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `InstrumentSerif-Regular.ttf` | Instrument Serif 400 | Google Fonts, `instrumentserif/v5` |
| `Geist-Regular.ttf` | Geist 400 (static instance) | Google Fonts, `geist/v5` |
| `GeistMono-Regular.ttf` | Geist Mono 400 (static instance) | Google Fonts, `geistmono/v6` |

All three are OFL 1.1.

Google Fonts serves woff2 to a modern user agent and TTF only to one it
believes is old, so re-fetching means asking for the TTF explicitly:

```bash
UA="Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; U; Android 4.0.3; en-us) AppleWebKit/534.30 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/4.0 Mobile Safari/534.30"
curl -s -H "User-Agent: $UA" "https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Instrument+Serif" | grep -o 'https://fonts.gstatic.com[^)]*'
```

Check the first four bytes of anything you download: `00010000` is a
real TrueType file. The legacy-IE user agent returns an EOT instead,
which is the wrong format and fails at render time rather than at
download time.

research.body:
# saake.dev — implementation plans

Five layers, four sub-layers each. **Twenty plans.** Each sub-layer gets its own document with objectives, prerequisites, step-by-step tasks, acceptance criteria, and rollback.

Layers are ordered by dependency. Sub-layers within a layer are mostly parallel but numbered in the order they should start.

---

## Layer 1 — Foundation

Infrastructure and the token layer. Nothing renders until this is right.

| # | Plan | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | [Domain & deployment repair](01-foundation/1.1-domain-deployment.md) | `saake.dev` resolves to a live deployment |
| 1.2 | [Repo reset & scaffold](01-foundation/1.2-repo-scaffold.md) | Clean Next.js App Router tree, git initialized, branch strategy |
| 1.3 | [Token layer](01-foundation/1.3-token-layer.md) | Every value in `design/system.md` as CSS custom properties + Tailwind config |
| 1.4 | [Fonts & CI guardrails](01-foundation/1.4-fonts-ci.md) | Self-hosted faces; CI fails on off-token values |

## Layer 2 — System in code

The design system becomes components. No page work starts until primitives exist.

| # | Plan | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 2.1 | [Primitives](02-system/2.1-primitives.md) | `Rule` `Label` `SectionHead` `Prose` `Grain` `ExternalLink` |
| 2.2 | [Motion](02-system/2.2-motion.md) | Reveal primitive, `html.js` gate, reduced-motion, hover gesture |
| 2.3 | [Composites](02-system/2.3-composites.md) | `MortarGrid` `ProjectCard` `SpecTable` `Figure` `Footnote` |
| 2.4 | [Shell](02-system/2.4-shell.md) | Nav, footer, skip link, focus management, theme toggle |

## Layer 3 — Content

The hardest layer and the one that decides whether the site is credible.

| # | Plan | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | [Fabrication purge](03-content/3.1-fabrication-purge.md) | Every invented claim deleted; audit log of what was removed |
| 3.2 | [Content schema](03-content/3.2-schema.md) | Typed case-study model with required `problem`/`response`/`outcome` |
| 3.3 | [Project ground truth](03-content/3.3-ground-truth.md) | What each real project actually does, verified, with live-status checks |
| 3.4 | [Editorial voice](03-content/3.4-editorial-voice.md) | Pronoun partition, jargon gradient, tagline frame; all copy written |

## Layer 4 — Pages

| # | Plan | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | [Home](04-pages/4.1-home.md) | Position → Demonstrate → Prove → Humanize → Qualify → Corroborate → Ask |
| 4.2 | [Work index & case template](04-pages/4.2-work.md) | Index + the repeating case-study template, SSR with correct canonicals |
| 4.3 | [The flagship argument](04-pages/4.3-flagship.md) | The one long case study — this site's own rebuild |
| 4.4 | [About & contact](04-pages/4.4-about-contact.md) | Real identity, real channels, no fabricated availability |

## Layer 5 — Quality & launch

| # | Plan | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 5.1 | [Accessibility](05-quality/5.1-accessibility.md) | The ten-point floor, verified with axe + manual keyboard pass |
| 5.2 | [Performance & SEO](05-quality/5.2-performance-seo.md) | Core Web Vitals, metadata, sitemap, OG images, structured data |
| 5.3 | [QA](05-quality/5.3-qa.md) | Cross-browser, device matrix, both themes, no-JS, reduced-motion |
| 5.4 | [Launch](05-quality/5.4-launch.md) | Cutover, redirects, monitoring, post-launch checklist |

---

## Critical path

```
1.1 ──────────────────────────────────────────────► 5.4
1.2 → 1.3 → 1.4 → 2.1 → 2.2 → 2.3 → 2.4 ─┐
                                          ├─► 4.1 → 4.2 → 4.3 → 4.4 → 5.1 → 5.2 → 5.3 → 5.4
3.1 → 3.3 → 3.2 → 3.4 ────────────────────┘
```

**1.1 is independent** — the domain can be fixed today, in parallel with everything.

**Layer 3 runs parallel to Layer 2.** Content research doesn't need components. This is the schedule's main lever: 3.3 (finding out what the projects actually do) is the longest-lead item and the only one that needs the user, so it starts immediately.

**4.3 blocks launch.** The flagship argument is the credential. A site with twelve inventories and no argument misses the entire point of the positioning.

---

## Blocking unknowns

Carried into 3.3 and 4.4. **3.3's verification pass resolved #2; direct confirmation from Aryan resolved #1; live API checks resolved #4.** See 3.3 for the evidence and the full 18-question list.

1. ~~**How to credit the user.**~~ **Resolved 2026-08-02, confirmed directly.** Name is **Aryan**, online handle **saake**, occasional nickname **ary**. Both repo data files were wrong (`saake-engine.json` said `Sake`, `skills.ts` said `Saake`) and the `Ari` guess was close but incorrect. Unblocks P15's tagline frame, the about-page byline, and 5.2's JSON-LD `Person` node.
2. ~~**What the projects do.**~~ **Resolved by source reading.** `waveline` is real and non-trivial (server-side Spotify OAuth with JWT sessions, live Web Audio frequency analysis, Konva canvas). `SkillBridge` is the largest codebase but ships a CSR-only shell — 1,119 bytes of HTML whose entire text is "You need to enable JavaScript to run this app." `esp32-home-automation` is coherent firmware plus nine hardware docs. Remaining question is narrower and specific: **was the ESP32 ever physically assembled?** Nothing in the repo answers it, and it decides whether the project ships as a built system or as a design.
3. **Correct LinkedIn URL** — `linkedin.com/in/saake` is unverified. Also gates 5.2's `Person.sameAs`, which ships with GitHub only until confirmed. Same for Twitter/X, whose existence is unconfirmed.
4. ~~**Does `hello@saake.dev` receive mail.**~~ **Resolved — it does not exist**, and the zone's catch-all is disabled, so mail to it is rejected. **`hi@saake.dev` is live** and forwards to `saakedev@gmail.com`. 4.4 corrected.
5. **Which projects to feature**, and whether `sentinal` / `LoveQuest` belong.

Confirmed already: `github.com/RealSaake` is correct (`github.com/saake` in `social-links.tsx` is wrong). `eostrails.com` and `tools.saake.dev` do not resolve and are cut.

### The site is live, and serving the old build

`saake.dev` resolves and returns 200 as of 2026-08-02 — the DNS repair was the entire fix. What it serves is the **pre-rebuild site with its fabrications intact**. Verified against live HTML:

- **`/contact` publishes `+1 (555) 123-4567`, `San Francisco`, a 24-hour response promise, and `github.com/saake`.** Invented phone, invented location, invented SLA, wrong profile URL.
- **All six live routes canonicalize to `https://saake.dev/`** — 4.2's headline defect, confirmed in production rather than inferred.
- **That canonical target 308s to `www.saake.dev`**, so every page names a canonical that is not a 200.

This does not change the plan order; it changes the urgency. Either ship the rebuild or take `/contact` down. Full detail: `ops/infrastructure.md` and 5.4.

**Open decision, blocked on Vercel dashboard access:** the apex 308s to `www`, which is the inverse of the intent. Apex is preferred. Until it is settled, 5.2's `metadataBase` cannot be written correctly. The available Vercel token authenticates but has zero project scope, so this is a dashboard action.

### Two findings from 3.3 that change other plans

**The fabrication is not confined to the site.** The project READMEs carry the same inflation. `waveline`'s homepage advertises "2048 FFT Resolution"; `useSpotifyPlayer.ts:204` sets `fftSize = 256`, and `2048` appears in exactly one place in that codebase — `page.tsx:104`, as display text. Its "AI Visual DNA" is a character-code hash returning an HSL string. `SkillBridge`'s README asserts it "has achieved TECHNOLOGICAL SINGULARITY."

Consequence: **linking a repo publishes its README.** Cleaning the README of every featured project is a prerequisite for featuring it, not a launch-day task. Replacement copy is sourced from code, never from a README.

**Unrelated and urgent.** `LoveQuest` has `.env` (97 B) and `kat_engine/.env` (461 B) committed to a public repo. Contents deliberately not read. Any key in them should be treated as compromised and rotated; deleting the files in a new commit does not remove them from history. This is independent of the rebuild and should not wait for it.

---

## Standing rules

Apply to every plan; not repeated in each.

- **No fabricated content, ever.** No invented numbers, dates, roles, credentials, locations, or metrics. If a fact isn't verified, it doesn't ship.
- **Accessibility is merge-blocking**, not a Layer 5 cleanup. 5.1 verifies a floor that was held from commit one.
- **Token discipline.** No hex literals, no arbitrary values, no off-scale sizes in components.
- **Every route SSR'd** with a correct self-referential canonical.
- **Each plan ends green** — a sub-layer isn't done until its acceptance criteria pass and the site still builds.

research.excerpt: Layer: 5 — Quality and launch · Depends on: 5.1, 5.2 · Blocks: 5.4
research.body:
# 5.3 — QA

**Layer:** 5 — Quality and launch · **Depends on:** 5.1, 5.2 · **Blocks:** 5.4

---

## Objective

Verify the site behaves correctly across browsers, devices, themes, and the two degraded modes it explicitly promises to support: **no JavaScript** and **reduced motion**.

5.1 proved the accessibility floor. 5.2 proved metadata and speed. This plan covers what neither does: **does it actually look and work right in conditions nobody develops in.**

**The scope boundary matters.** 5.1 and 5.2 own correctness properties that are machine-checkable and already enforced in CI. This plan owns the things that require a human to look: does the layout hold at 320px, does the dark theme read as designed rather than merely pass contrast, does the reveal fire once rather than on every scroll. Where they overlap — no-JS, reduced motion — this plan checks the *visual and behavioural* outcome while 5.1 checks the *assertable* one. Both are needed; neither substitutes.

---

## Prerequisites

- 5.1 green: zero axe violations, keyboard and NVDA records complete.
- 5.2 green: `verify:seo` passing, budgets met.
- `tests/fixtures/routes.json` frozen — the same inventory all three plans consume.
- Production build running locally, plus a preview deployment for real-device testing.
- Playwright with Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit installed.

---

## Steps

### Step 1 — The matrix

Full cross-product is combinatorial nonsense. This is stratified: **automated where cheap and deterministic, manual where a human eye is the instrument.**

**Automated — every cell, every route, in CI:**

| Axis | Values |
|---|---|
| Engine | Chromium, Firefox, WebKit |
| Theme | light, dark |
| Viewport | 320, 390, 768, 1280, 1920 |
| Mode | default, no-JS, reduced-motion |

Playwright covers all three engines, which is the reason to lean on it: WebKit is the engine most likely to break and the one least likely to be on a Windows dev machine.

**Manual — a deliberately short list, because manual passes that are long do not get run:**

| Device | Browser | Why this one |
|---|---|---|
| A real Android phone | Chrome | Aryan has one. Real cellular, real touch, real thumb reach |
| A real iPhone *or* BrowserStack iOS | Safari | **The one that will break.** See step 5 |
| Windows 11 desktop | Chrome, Firefox, Edge | The dev machine — free to check |
| Windows 11 desktop | 200% OS scaling | Catches viewport-unit and fixed-height bugs invisibly at 100% |

macOS Safari and Chrome are not in the manual list — WebKit via Playwright covers the engine, and no Mac is available. **Recorded as a gap rather than quietly skipped**: desktop Safari's viewport and font rendering differ from Playwright WebKit in small ways, so a Safari-specific visual bug could ship. Acceptable for a personal site; not acceptable to leave undocumented.

### Step 2 — Visual regression, with a deliberate limit

Screenshot every route × theme × viewport, compare against approved baselines.

```ts
// tests/visual.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test'
import routes from './fixtures/routes.json' assert { type: 'json' }

const VIEWPORTS = [
  { name: '320',  width: 320,  height: 800 },
  { name: '390',  width: 390,  height: 844 },
  { name: '768',  width: 768,  height: 1024 },
  { name: '1280', width: 1280, height: 900 },
  { name: '1920', width: 1920, height: 1080 },
]

for (const route of routes) {
  for (const theme of ['light', 'dark'] as const) {
    for (const vp of VIEWPORTS) {
      test(`visual ${route.path} [${theme}/${vp.name}]`, async ({ page }) => {
        await page.setViewportSize(vp)
        await page.addInitScript(t => {
          localStorage.setItem('theme', t)
          document.documentElement.dataset.theme = t
        }, theme)
        await page.goto(route.path, { waitUntil: 'networkidle' })

        // reveals are IntersectionObserver-driven; settle them before capture
        await page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight))
        await page.waitForTimeout(800)          // --dur-enter 640ms + margin
        await page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, 0))
        await page.waitForTimeout(200)

        await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot(`${route.name}-${theme}-${vp.name}.png`, {
          fullPage: true,
          maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01,
        })
      })
    }
  }
}
```

**Two things this will get wrong if not handled.**

The grain layer is `feTurbulence`, and SVG filter rasterization differs across engines and even across driver versions. At `--grain: .012` the difference is sub-perceptual but not sub-pixel-diff. **Baselines are per-engine** (Playwright does this by default via platform suffixes), and `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01` absorbs the rest. If grain diffs still cause noise, mask the grain element rather than raising the threshold — a high global threshold hides real regressions.

The reveal settle above is a `waitForTimeout`, which is a smell. It is used deliberately: the alternative is waiting on an animation-complete signal that 2.2's CSS-only reveal does not emit. If flake appears, add a `data-revealed="true"` attribute in the reveal primitive's transition-end handler and wait on that instead — a small change to 2.2 that makes this deterministic.

**Baseline updates require review.** `--update-snapshots` on a PR is how an unnoticed regression becomes the new normal. Diff images go in the PR; a human approves the change or rejects it.

### Step 3 — No-JS

The site promises this. 2.2 ships an `html.js` gate specifically so content is visible without JavaScript.

```ts
test.describe('no-JS', () => {
  test.use({ javaScriptEnabled: false })

  for (const route of routes) {
    test(`renders without JS: ${route.path}`, async ({ page }) => {
      await page.goto(route.path)

      await expect(page.locator('h1')).toBeVisible()
      await expect(page.locator('h1')).toHaveText(route.h1)
      await expect(page.locator('main')).toBeVisible()

      // reveal content must be VISIBLE, not merely present
      for (const el of await page.locator('.reveal').all()) {
        await expect(el).toBeVisible()
        const opacity = await el.evaluate(n => getComputedStyle(n).opacity)
        expect(opacity).toBe('1')
      }

      // navigation still works — it is anchors, not a router
      const nav = page.locator('header nav a').first()
      await expect(nav).toHaveAttribute('href', /.+/)

      // grain is SSR'd, so it is present without JS
      await expect(page.locator('[data-grain]')).toBeAttached()
    })
  }
})
```

**What must degrade gracefully rather than work:**

| Feature | No-JS behaviour | Acceptable? |
|---|---|---|
| Reveal animations | Content visible immediately, unanimated | Yes — this is the `html.js` gate working |
| Theme toggle | Non-functional; site renders in the SSR default | Yes, with a caveat below |
| Mobile menu | **Must still expose navigation** | Only if nav links are reachable — see below |
| Page transitions | None | Yes — decorative |
| Contact | `mailto:` link | Yes — 4.4 chose `mailto` over a form partly for this |

**The mobile menu is the real risk.** If it is a JS-toggled overlay, a no-JS visitor at 390px has no navigation at all — the site becomes a set of unreachable pages. Two acceptable resolutions: a CSS-only disclosure (checkbox or `<details>`), or nav links rendered visibly in the footer so they are always reachable. **Assert the second regardless**, because it is cheap and it makes the failure mode impossible:

```ts
test('footer nav reachable without JS at 390px', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 390, height: 844 })
  await page.goto('/')
  const links = page.locator('footer a[href^="/"]')
  expect(await links.count()).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3)
  for (const l of await links.all()) await expect(l).toBeVisible()
})
```

**The theme caveat.** With no JS, `localStorage.theme` cannot be read, so the site renders in whatever the SSR default is. That is correct and unavoidable. What must not happen is a **flash** — the inline theme script in `<head>` (2.4) resolves the theme before first paint when JS *is* available, and its absence must not leave a half-applied state. Verify the no-JS render is fully and consistently one theme, not a mixture.

### Step 4 — Reduced motion

```ts
test.describe('reduced motion', () => {
  test.use({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })

  for (const route of routes) {
    test(`reduced motion: ${route.path}`, async ({ page }) => {
      await page.goto(route.path)

      for (const el of await page.locator('.reveal').all()) {
        await expect(el).toBeVisible()
        const s = await el.evaluate(n => {
          const c = getComputedStyle(n)
          return { opacity: c.opacity, transform: c.transform, transition: c.transitionDuration }
        })
        expect(s.opacity).toBe('1')
        expect(s.transform).toBe('none')
      }

      const infinite = await page.evaluate(() =>
        [...document.querySelectorAll('*')]
          .filter(n => getComputedStyle(n).animationIterationCount === 'infinite').length)
      expect(infinite).toBe(0)
    })
  }
})
```

**The distinction that matters, and the one the reference corpus got wrong:** reduced motion means *content is visible without animation*, not *the animation is removed and the content stays at its pre-animation state*. A reveal that starts at `opacity: 0` and has its transition disabled leaves the content permanently invisible — a strictly worse outcome than the animation. The assertion is `opacity: 1`, never merely "no transition."

Hover states (`.lift`) may keep their `--dur-act: 160ms` transition under reduced motion. That preference targets vestibular triggers — large-scale motion, parallax, autoplay — not a 160ms border shift on deliberate interaction. Removing every transition makes an interface feel broken, which is not what the user asked for.

### Step 5 — Safari and WebKit specifics

The engine most likely to break, and the one hardest to test from Windows. Each item below is a known WebKit divergence, checked explicitly:

| # | Check | Why WebKit specifically |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `100vh` on mobile Safari | Includes the URL bar; content gets clipped. Use `100dvh` with a `100vh` fallback |
| 2 | `position: fixed` grain layer during scroll | WebKit has historically repainted fixed layers oddly on rubber-band scroll |
| 3 | `backdrop-filter`, if used anywhere | Needs `-webkit-` prefix; check the built CSS, not the source |
| 4 | `feTurbulence` grain rendering | Different rasterization; confirm it is texture, not visible banding |
| 5 | `woff2` + `font-display: swap` | Confirm no invisible-text period and no double swap |
| 6 | Focus ring visibility | Safari's default focus behaviour differs; 5.1's 2px `--focus` ring must render |
| 7 | Date/number formatting in case-study metadata | `Intl` output differs subtly between engines |
| 8 | Smooth scroll on skip link | Safari support for `scroll-behavior` has been inconsistent |
| 9 | `mailto:` link on iOS | Opens Mail; confirm the address is correct and prefilled subject survives |
| 10 | Rubber-band overscroll | Confirm no white gap below the footer where `--paper` should be |

Items 1, 2, 9, and 10 are **only** observable on a real iOS device — Playwright WebKit does not reproduce mobile Safari's chrome behaviour. Either borrow an iPhone or use BrowserStack for one session. **This is the single highest-value manual test in the plan**, because it is the only condition where a first-impression visitor could see something plainly broken.

### Step 6 — Theme switching

Beyond 5.1's contrast assertions, verify the mechanism:

| # | Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | First visit, OS light | Light theme, **no flash** |
| 2 | First visit, OS dark | Dark theme, **no flash** |
| 3 | Toggle → reload | Choice persists via `localStorage.theme` |
| 4 | Set "system", change OS theme while open | Site follows live, without reload |
| 5 | Set explicit light, change OS to dark |

research.body:
# 5.2 — Performance & SEO

**Layer:** 5 — Quality and launch · **Depends on:** 1.4, 2.2, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 5.1 · **Blocks:** 5.3, 5.4

---

## Objective

Make the site fast on a real phone on real cellular data, and make every page independently discoverable, correctly attributed, and honestly described in its own markup.

Three earlier plans deferred specific work to this one, and those debts are the spine of it:

| Owed to | What was deferred |
|---|---|
| 4.1 | CI assertion that `alternates` never appears in a layout file |
| 4.2 | Script proving no two routes share a canonical |
| 4.4 / `ops/infrastructure.md` | JSON-LD `Person` node, built from verified identity only |

Plus one item that was not deferred but has become blocking since: **`metadataBase` cannot be written correctly until the canonical-host question is settled**, because the apex currently 308s to `www`.

**This plan does not chase a Lighthouse score.** A 100 on a warm desktop run proves nothing about the visitor this site exists for — someone opening a link on a phone, on cellular, once. Field data over lab data wherever the two disagree, and where only lab data exists, it runs throttled.

---

## Prerequisites

- 4.1–4.4 complete; all routes render and build green.
- 5.1 green, including `tests/fixtures/routes.json` — **the frozen route inventory is this plan's input too.** One inventory, checked by both plans, so a route cannot be accessible-but-unindexed or indexed-but-untested.
- 1.4's `verify` chain in place (`verify:tokens`, `verify:fonts`, `lint:css`, `lint:js`, chained ahead of `next build`). This plan adds `verify:seo` to it.
- Trailing-slash decision from 1.2, asserted in 4.2 step 5. **Whichever value ships, every canonical string must match the served URL byte for byte.**
- Lighthouse CI and Playwright installed. Chromium for both.

### Blocking decision — the canonical host

Live as of 2026-08-02:

```
http://saake.dev        → 301 → https://saake.dev
https://saake.dev       → 308 → https://www.saake.dev/
https://www.saake.dev   → 200
```

**`www` is currently the host that serves.** The intended canonical is the apex. Until that is reconciled in the Vercel dashboard, `metadataBase` cannot be written without either being wrong or codifying the wrong host.

The rule this plan enforces, whichever way it goes: **`metadataBase` names the host that returns 200 without a redirect hop.** A canonical pointing at a 308 is not a canonical — it hands the crawler a forwarding address and asks it to resolve the ambiguity the markup was supposed to remove.

Preferred: set apex primary in Vercel, `www` redirects to it, `metadataBase = https://saake.dev`. Fallback: accept `www`, `metadataBase = https://www.saake.dev`. **Not acceptable: the present state**, where the live build canonicalizes every route to `https://saake.dev/` and that URL redirects.

This is a dashboard action and the available Vercel token cannot perform it — same access gap as 5.4.

---

## Steps

### Step 1 — Metadata: one base, per-route overrides, zero inheritance

**Root layout carries `metadataBase` and defaults. It carries no `alternates` key at all.**

```ts
// app/layout.tsx
import type { Metadata } from 'next'

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  metadataBase: new URL(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? 'https://saake.dev'),
  title: {
    default: 'Aryan — design and engineering',
    template: '%s — Aryan',
  },
  description: '…',            // 3.4 writes this; no jargon, no metrics
  openGraph: { type: 'website', locale: 'en_US', siteName: 'saake.dev' },
  twitter: { card: 'summary_large_image' },
  robots: { index: true, follow: true },
  // NO alternates. Ever. Enforced by verify:seo.
}
```

`NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` exists so preview deployments canonicalize to themselves rather than to production. A preview that canonicalizes to production tells the crawler the preview *is* production; a preview that canonicalizes to a preview URL is harmless because previews are `noindex` anyway (step 6).

**Every route sets its own canonical in its own `generateMetadata`.** 4.1 established the pattern, 4.2 applied it per slug, 4.4 applied it to `/about` and `/contact`. This plan's contribution is proving it held.

The failure being prevented is specific and was live in production: the old build set `alternates: { canonical: '/' }` once in the root layout and never overrode it, so all six routes — including every case study — instructed crawlers to attribute them to the homepage. Confirmed against live HTML, not inferred:

```
/          → canonical https://saake.dev/
/about     → canonical https://saake.dev/
/contact   → canonical https://saake.dev/
/projects  → canonical https://saake.dev/
```

A portfolio whose case studies de-index themselves is not a portfolio. **This is the single highest-value item in Layer 5.**

### Step 2 — `verify:seo`, the script that makes it structural

Assertions in a test file get skipped when the suite is red for unrelated reasons. This runs in the `verify` chain ahead of `next build`, so a canonical defect fails the build rather than a test.

**File: `scripts/verify-seo.mjs`**

Run against a built server on `localhost:3000`, iterating `tests/fixtures/routes.json`.

| # | Assertion | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `grep -rn "alternates" app/**/layout.tsx` → no match | 4.1's debt. A layout-level canonical silently overrides nothing and inherits everywhere |
| 2 | Every route emits **exactly one** `<link rel="canonical">` | Two canonicals is undefined behaviour |
| 3 | Each canonical is **absolute** and **self-referential** | Relative canonicals resolve against the requesting URL, which defeats the purpose |
| 4 | **No two routes share a canonical** | 4.2's debt. This is the assertion that would have caught the live defect |
| 5 | Each canonical, fetched, returns **200 with zero redirects** | Catches the apex/`www` mismatch and any trailing-slash drift |
| 6 | Canonical string matches the served URL byte for byte | `/work/x` and `/work/x/` are different URLs to a crawler |
| 7 | Sitemap URL set **equals** the route inventory, exactly | Drift in either direction is a defect: unlisted route or listed-but-dead URL |
| 8 | Every route has a non-empty, unique `<title>` and `<meta name="description">` | Duplicate titles across case studies is the commonest self-inflicted SEO wound |
| 9 | Every route emits a valid `og:image` that returns 200 | A broken OG image fails silently and only in someone else's chat window |
| 10 | JSON-LD on every route parses as JSON and has `@context` + `@type` | Malformed structured data is worse than none |
| 11 | Raw HTML contains the route's `h1` text **pre-hydration** | SSR proof, in bytes. Overlaps 5.1 deliberately — both plans depend on it |

```js
// scripts/verify-seo.mjs  (sketch — assertions above are the contract)
import routes from '../tests/fixtures/routes.json' with { type: 'json' }

const BASE = process.env.VERIFY_BASE ?? 'http://localhost:3000'
const errors = []
const canonicals = new Map()

for (const route of routes) {
  const res  = await fetch(`${BASE}${route.path}`, { redirect: 'manual' })
  const html = await res.text()

  if (res.status !== 200) errors.push(`${route.path}: expected 200, got ${res.status}`)

  const found = [...html.matchAll(/<link[^>]+rel="canonical"[^>]+href="([^"]+)"/g)].map(m => m[1])
  if (found.length !== 1) {
    errors.push(`${route.path}: expected 1 canonical, found ${found.length}`)
    continue
  }
  const [canonical] = found

  if (!canonical.startsWith('http')) errors.push(`${route.path}: canonical not absolute — ${canonical}`)
  if (canonical !== route.canonical) errors.push(`${route.path}: canonical ${canonical} !== ${route.canonical}`)

  const prev = canonicals.get(canonical)
  if (prev) errors.push(`DUPLICATE canonical ${canonical} on ${prev} and ${route.path}`)
  canonicals.set(canonical, route.path)

  // the canonical must itself be a 200, not a redirect
  const head = await fetch(canonical, { method: 'HEAD', redirect: 'manual' })
  if (head.status !== 200) {
    errors.push(`${route.path}: canonical ${canonical} returns ${head.status} (must be 200, no hop)`)
  }

  if (!html.includes(route.h1)) errors.push(`${route.path}: h1 "${route.h1}" absent from raw HTML (CSR?)`)
}

// sitemap parity — both directions
const sitemap = await (await fetch(`${BASE}/sitemap.xml`)).text()
const listed  = new Set([...sitemap.matchAll(/<loc>([^<]+)<\/loc>/g)].map(m => m[1]))
const expected = new Set(routes.map(r => r.canonical))
for (const u of expected) if (!listed.has(u))   errors.push(`sitemap missing ${u}`)
for (const u of listed)   if (!expected.has(u)) errors.push(`sitemap lists unknown ${u}`)

console.log(errors.length ? errors.join('\n') : `verify-seo: ok (${routes.length} routes)`)
process.exit(errors.length ? 1 : 0)
```

Wire into 1.4's chain:

```json
"verify:seo": "node scripts/verify-seo.mjs",
"verify": "npm run verify:tokens && npm run verify:fonts && npm run lint:css && npm run lint:js"
```

`verify:seo` needs a running server, so it cannot sit in the pre-build chain. It runs in CI after `next build && next start`, and it is a **required check** — same status as 5.1's `accessibility` job.

### Step 3 — Sitemap and robots, generated from the content collection

Both are generated from the same typed collection that generates the routes. Hand-maintained lists drift, and the drift is invisible until a case study silently stops being indexed.

```ts
// app/sitemap.ts
import type { MetadataRoute } from 'next'
import { caseStudies } from '@/content'

const BASE = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? 'https://saake.dev'

export default function sitemap(): MetadataRoute.Sitemap {
  const staticRoutes = ['', '/work', '/about', '/contact'].map(p => ({
    url: `${BASE}${p}`,
    lastModified: new Date(),
    changeFrequency: 'monthly' as const,
    priority: p === '' ? 1 : 0.8,
  }))

  const studies = caseStudies.map(s => ({
    url: `${BASE}/work/${s.slug}`,
    lastModified: new Date(),
    changeFrequency: 'yearly' as const,
    priority: s.flagship ? 0.9 : 0.7,
  }))

  return [...staticRoutes, ...studies]
}
```

`priority` and `changeFrequency` are hints Google has said it largely ignores. They cost nothing and are set honestly rather than gamed — every URL at `1.0` is a well-known non-signal.

```ts
// app/robots.ts
import type { MetadataRoute } from 'next'

const BASE = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? 'https://saake.dev'

export default function robots(): MetadataRoute.Robots {
  return {
    rules: [{ userAgent: '*', allow: '/' }],
    sitemap: `${BASE}/sitemap.xml`,
    host: BASE,
  }
}
```

**One editorial decision to put to Aryan rather than decide here.** The studio in the reference corpus sets a `Content-Signal` header declaring `ai-train=no` and disallows several AI crawlers. That is a legitimate stance and a defensible one for a portfolio, since the work *is* the product. It is also a choice with tradeoffs — it does not meaningfully prevent training, and it forgoes some AI-surface discovery. **Default here is to allow everything**, because obscurity is the larger risk for a portfolio nobody has read yet. Flag the option; do not decide it silently.

### Step 4 — OG images

The single highest-leverage visual asset on the site, because it is what appears when a link is pasted into Slack, iMessage, or a DM — often before anyone visits.

**Generate at build time via `ImageResponse`, one per route**, so a case study cannot ship without one.

```tsx
// app/work/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx
import { ImageResponse } from 'next/og'
import { getCaseStudy } from '@/content'

export const size = { width: 1200, height: 630 }
export const contentType = 'image/png'

export default async function Image({ params }: { params: { slug: string } }) {
  const study = getCaseStudy(params.slug)

research.body:
# 5.4 — Launch

**Layer:** 5 — Quality and launch · **Depends on:** all nineteen preceding plans · **Blocks:** nothing

---

## Objective

Get the rebuilt site live at `saake.dev`, with every earlier plan's acceptance criteria green, and with a rollback that takes one action.

This plan is unusual in that its hardest problem is already solved, and solved more simply than a previous session concluded. The DNS repair during the infrastructure pass was the entire fix: `saake.dev` resolves and serves 200. What it serves is the **old, fabricated build** — so this plan's real subject is a deployment swap behind a working domain, not a cutover.

**Launch is not a milestone that makes the site done.** It is the moment the site becomes checkable by strangers. Everything in 4.3's argument depends on the shipped artifact surviving inspection, so the gate below is not ceremony — it is the last point at which a fabricated string or a broken canonical can be caught cheaply.

---

## Prerequisites

- Plans 1.1 through 5.3, all acceptance criteria green.
- Cloudflare access (DNS is Cloudflare; registrar is Namecheap).
- **Vercel access with team scope** — see Step 1. The token from earlier sessions is insufficient and this is now understood rather than mysterious.
- `curl` and `node`. Python is not installed.

### Verified state — 2026-08-02, after the DNS repair

**The domain resolves. The DNS repair was the whole fix.**

| Host | Status |
|---|---|
| `saake.dev` | **308 → `https://www.saake.dev/`** |
| `www.saake.dev` | **200**, `x-vercel-cache: HIT`, served from `bom1` |
| `http://saake.dev` | **301 → https** (`always_use_https` now on) |
| `saakedev.vercel.app` | **200** |
| `sake.dev` (one 'a') | does not resolve; not owned, not needed |

DNS points both apex and `www` at `saakedev.vercel.app`, proxied through Cloudflare. Pre-change snapshot: `ops/dns-backup-pre-cutover.json`. **The apex 308s to `www`**, so `www` is the de-facto canonical host — the opposite of what Step 2 below specifies. See Step 2.3.

### Correction — the earlier `Host`-header diagnosis was wrong

An earlier pass concluded that `saake.dev` was not registered on any Vercel project and that the remaining fix was attaching the domain. That was incorrect, and the reasoning is worth keeping because the error is a subtle one that will otherwise be repeated.

Two pieces of evidence supported it, and both were misread:

1. **`curl -H "Host: saake.dev" https://saakedev.vercel.app` → 404.** This looked like proof that Vercel had no mapping for the hostname. It is not. TLS is negotiated against `saakedev.vercel.app` via SNI, so the edge resolves the request in *that* project's routing context and then sees a `Host` it does not serve there. The same command today returns **403** while `saake.dev` itself serves 200 — the test's output changed while the thing it claimed to measure did not. **A test whose result moves independently of the property under test is not a diagnostic.** Do not use it.

2. **`GET /v6/domains/saake.dev` → `not_found`.** Read as "not registered anywhere." It actually means "not found *within this token's scope*" — and the token's scope is empty (see below). An empty-scope token returns `not_found` for every domain in existence, including ones that plainly work.

The real cause was the one identified first and then talked past: the apex `CNAME` pointed at `saake-portfolio.vercel.app`, which does not exist, and `www` pointed at a stale deployment-specific hostname. Repointing both at `saakedev.vercel.app` fixed it. The delay between the change and the site working was ordinary propagation, and the `Host`-header test run inside that window manufactured a second, fictional root cause.

**The general lesson, which is the part worth keeping:** when a fix is applied and the symptom persists, the two hypotheses are "the fix was wrong" and "the fix has not taken effect yet." Reaching for a clever diagnostic before eliminating propagation produced a confident, wrong, and expensive answer. Wait out the TTL first.

**Token limitation (still true, now correctly interpreted):** the Vercel token authenticates as `realsaake` but returns **zero projects** and `forbidden` on `/v2/teams`. The project is in a team scope the token does not cover. The consequence is narrower than previously stated: it does not mean anything is misconfigured, only that **this token cannot be used to verify or change Vercel-side settings**. Deploys, domain settings, and redirect configuration need dashboard access or a team-scoped token.

### What is actually live — the old build

The domain works and serves the **pre-rebuild site, fabrications intact**. Verified against live HTML:

| Route | Status | Canonical served |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | 200 | `https://saake.dev/` |
| `/about` | 200 | `https://saake.dev/` |
| `/contact` | 200 | `https://saake.dev/` |
| `/projects` | 200 | `https://saake.dev/` |
| `/work` | **404** | `https://saake.dev/` |
| `/blog` | **404** | `https://saake.dev/` |

Three defects, all live right now:

- **`/contact` carries `+1 (555) 123-4567`, `San Francisco`, a 24-hour response promise, and `github.com/saake`** — the invented phone number, the invented location, the invented SLA, and a profile URL that is wrong (`RealSaake` is correct). Every one is on 4.4's deletion list.
- **Every route canonicalizes to `https://saake.dev/`.** This is 4.2's headline defect, confirmed in production rather than inferred from source.
- **The canonical points at a URL that 308s away.** `https://saake.dev/` redirects to `https://www.saake.dev/`, so every page declares a canonical that is not a `200`. Worse than the flat-canonical bug alone, and invisible without following the chain.

`/work` 404s while `/projects` serves, so the rebuilt route names do not match what is deployed — relevant to Step 3's redirect list, which now has at least one confirmed entry rather than a guess.

**This does not change the launch sequence; it changes its urgency.** The gate in Step 1 was written to run before a cutover. The cutover already happened by accident, so the site is currently publishing exactly the content 3.1 exists to delete. Either ship the rebuild or take `/contact` down — a live page with a fake phone number is worse than a missing one.

---

## Steps

### Step 1 — Pre-cutover gate

Every row must pass. A single failure stops the launch; none of these is a "fix it after" item, because each one is invisible to the person it misleads.

| # | Check | Command or method | Source plan |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | No fabricated strings in **built output** | grep below | 3.1 |
| 2 | Token layer intact | `node scripts/verify-tokens.mjs` | 1.3 |
| 3 | Fonts: 5 files, 3 faces, no synthetic bold | `node scripts/verify-fonts.mjs` | 1.4 |
| 4 | Exactly 2 lint-disable comments | `grep -rn "stylelint-disable\|eslint-disable" app/ components/ styles/ \| wc -l` | 1.4 |
| 5 | Types clean | `npx tsc --noEmit` | 3.2 |
| 6 | Content schema validates; every claim has `verified` | `npm run verify` | 3.2 |
| 7 | axe: zero violations, every route × both themes | Playwright suite | 5.1 |
| 8 | Keyboard traversal + NVDA pass recorded | manual, evidence logged | 5.1 |
| 9 | Canonicals self-referential in **SSR'd HTML** | curl below | 5.2 |
| 10 | Core Web Vitals within target | Lighthouse, throttled | 5.2 |
| 11 | No-JS: every route renders, content visible | Playwright `javaScriptEnabled: false` | 5.3 |
| 12 | Reduced-motion: content visible, no infinite loops | 5.3 matrix | 5.3 |
| 13 | Both themes, no FOUC, all viewports | 5.3 matrix | 5.3 |
| 14 | Every external link → 200 | loop below | 4.4 |
| 15 | Contact address receives a real test message | send one, confirm arrival | 4.4 |
| 16 | Featured repos' READMEs cleaned | manual review | 3.3 |

**Row 1 — the fabrication sweep, against `.next/`, not `src/`:**

```bash
grep -rniE "500000|2847|12543|hackermanQuotient|San Francisco|\(555\)|Tech Innovation|eostrails|tools\.saake\.dev|github\.com/saake|50k monthly|hello@saake\.dev|2048 FFT|linkedin\.com/in/saake" .next/server .next/static && echo "FABRICATION FOUND — BLOCKED" || echo "clean"
```

Grepping the build rather than the source is the whole point: source can be clean while a stale string survives in a cached chunk, a generated route manifest, or an OG image. The site is served from `.next/`, so `.next/` is what gets audited.

Two additions to the original 3.1 list, both found after it was written: `hello@saake.dev` (never existed — the working address is `hi@saake.dev`) and `2048 FFT` (waveline's homepage claim, contradicted by `fftSize = 256` in its own source).

**Row 9 — canonicals in raw SSR output:**

```bash
for p in "" work about contact work/rebuilding-this-site; do
  printf "%-28s " "/$p"
  curl -s "https://saakedev.vercel.app/$p" | grep -o '<link rel="canonical"[^>]*>' || echo "MISSING"
done
```

Run against the preview host **before** promoting, then again against the live host after. Each must be self-referential **and must name a URL that returns 200** — see Step 2.3, since the apex currently 308s to `www`. A canonical that only appears after hydration is not a canonical, and a canonical pointing at a redirect is not one either. Both are checked in raw bytes for that reason.

The live build fails this check today: all six routes canonicalize to `https://saake.dev/`, which is both wrong per-route and a 308. That is the before-picture.

**Row 14 — external links:**

```bash
for u in https://github.com/RealSaake https://waveline.vercel.app https://skillbridgev1.vercel.app; do
  printf "%-42s " "$u"; curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -L --max-time 15 "$u"
done
```

All three returned 200 on 2026-08-02. Two are free-tier Vercel deployments and that is not durable — re-check at launch, and again in the post-launch passes.

### Step 2 — Cutover

The domain already resolves, so this is no longer a cutover in the DNS sense. It is a **deployment swap behind a working domain** — which is easier, lower-risk, and instantly reversible.

**1. Deploy to production, confirm on the Vercel hostname.** The build must be the one that passed Step 1. Verify on `*.vercel.app` before promoting — this isolates build problems from domain problems, and the domain is already known-good.

**2. Confirm `saake.dev` and `www.saake.dev` are attached to the project.** They demonstrably are, since both serve 200. No action expected; verify rather than assume, because the earlier session's conclusion here was wrong in the other direction.

**3. Decide the canonical host — and note the current state contradicts the intent.**

**Live behaviour today: `saake.dev` 308s to `www.saake.dev`.** The apex is the redirect *source*, not the destination.

The recommendation remains **apex** — `saake.dev` is shorter, it is what the brand is, it is what every existing reference and every canonical tag in the current build uses, and it is what appears in `hi@saake.dev`. Flipping the redirect direction so `www` → apex is the intended end state.

**But this is a Vercel-side setting, and the available token cannot read or change it.** So one of two things happens:

- **Preferred:** in the Vercel dashboard, set `saake.dev` as the primary domain and `www.saake.dev` to redirect to it. Then every canonical in the rebuild points at a `200` rather than a `308`.
- **Acceptable fallback:** leave `www` as primary and set `metadataBase: new URL('https://www.saake.dev')`. This is worse aesthetically and fine technically.

**What is not acceptable is the current state** — canonicals pointing at `https://saake.dev/` while that URL 308s to `www`. A canonical must name a URL that returns 200. Whichever host wins, `metadataBase` must match it exactly, and Step 1 row 9 must be re-run after the decision.

This is a genuine blocker on 5.2's acceptance criteria, and it is a dashboard action, not a code change.

**4. Certificates are already issued.** Both hosts serve valid HTTPS through Cloudflare. Nothing to wait for. (
